data: k7s implements a custom, tokenized design system (src/styles/tokens.css and src/styles/global.css) based on the design handoff in design/README.md.
data.typography#Typography:
k7s bundles all font assets locally as WOFF2 files via @fontsource packages, ensuring full offline capability with zero external network calls:
UI & Controls: IBM Plex Sans (400 Regular, 500 Medium, 600 SemiBold)
Tables, Code & Terminal: JetBrains Mono and IBM Plex Mono (400–700 with tabular number figures)
data.accessibility--focus-architecture#Access:
k7s follows strict accessibility guidelines:
Native Focus Rings: Distinct focus indicators (--focus-ring) appear on all interactive controls during keyboard navigation (:focus-visible).
Focus Trapping: Overlays (Settings, Command Palette, Create YAML, Kubeconfig QR) trap focus inside their modals and restore focus to the triggering element on close (src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts).
Screen Reader Semantics: Table columns use scope="col", sidebars use role="navigation", tabs follow the standard ARIA tablist/tab pattern, and live regions announce row counts and status changes.

data: The k7s frontend (src/) is built with React 19 and uses Zustand as its centralized state management solution.
data.store-slice-architecture#Store Slice Arc: To prevent store bloat and facilitate unit testing, the Zustand store is organized into modular slices (src/store/):
data.1-connectionslicets#1. connectionSlice.t: Manages multi-cluster metadata, active cluster ID (activeCid), connection lifecycle state (connected | connecting | stale | disconnected), and per-kind watcher health status (starting | live | backoff | forbidden | stopped).
data.2-dataslicets#2. dataSlice.ts:
Holds resource rows keyed by cluster ID and resource kind: resourceRows[cid][kind]: Map<uid, Row>.
Applies incoming upsert and delete deltas with minimal memory allocations.
Computes aggregated Problems across workloads with memoization to avoid re-evaluating unchanged kinds.
data.3-detailslicets#3. detailSlice.ts: Manages state for the currently opened detail panel: selected resource reference, active tab (logs | properties | yaml | diff | events | metrics | topology | shell | nodeshell), log stream filters, and YAML editing draft buffers.
data.4-navigationslicets#4. navigationSlice.t: Stores current navigation view (e.g. pods, deployments, overview, problems), active namespace filter (all or specific namespace), and table search query strings.
data.5-terminalslicets#5. terminalSlice.ts: Manages cluster-scoped kubectl terminal tabs, active PTY process handles, and open state.
data.virtualization--windowing-performance#Vi:
In clusters containing 5,000 to 10,000+ pods, rendering every row in the DOM would degrade scroll performance and consume excessive memory.k7s employs a lightweight, custom virtualization hook (src/components/table/useVirtualRows.ts):
Constant DOM Footprint: Renders only the visible rows plus an overscan buffer (typically 30–45 DOM nodes total).
Zero Layout Shifts: Uses absolute positioning with calculated translateY offsets based on a fixed row height (e.g. 32px).
Granular Memoization: Row components (TableRow.tsx) are wrapped in React.memo, preventing re-renders of rows whose cell values and tones have not changed.

data: A fundamental architectural strength of k7s is the Provider Seam (src/providers/). All communication between the UI components and the backend is abstracted behind the DataProvider interface (src/providers/types.ts).
data.the-dataprovider-contract#The DataProvid:
export interface DataProvider {
  // Cluster & Contexts
  listContexts(): Promise<ContextInfo[]>
  connect(cid: string): Promise<ClusterInfo>
  disconnect(cid: string): Promise<void>
  
  // Real-time Event Subscriptions
  onResourceUpdate(cid: string, cb: (update: ResourceUpdate) => void): Unsubscribe
  onClusterStatus(cid: string, cb: (status: ClusterStatus) => void): Unsubscribe
  onWatcherHealth(cid: string, cb: (health: WatcherHealthMap) => void): Unsubscribe
  onPodMetrics(cid: string, cb: (metrics: PodMetricsMap) => void): Unsubscribe
  
  // Resource Operations
  getYaml(ref: ResourceRef): Promise<string>
  dryRunYaml(ref: ResourceRef, yaml: string): Promise<DryRunResult>
  applyYaml(ref: ResourceRef, yaml: string): Promise<ApplyResult>
  deleteResource(ref: ResourceRef): Promise<void>
  scaleResource(ref: ResourceRef, replicas: number): Promise<void>
  restartWorkload(ref: ResourceRef): Promise<void>
  
  // Logs & Shells
  startLogStream(ref: ResourceRef, opts: LogStreamOptions, onLine: (line: LogLine) => void): Promise<LogHandle>
  startTerminalSession(opts: TerminalSpawnOptions): Promise<TerminalHandle>
}
data.1-tauriprovider-srcproviderstauritauripr:
The production provider used inside the Tauri desktop app.
Maps method calls to Tauri IPC commands (invoke('connect', { ... })) and subscribes to Tauri events (listen('resource-update', ...)).
data.2-mockprovider-srcprovidersmockmockprovi:
Used in browser development (VITE_DEMO=1) and automated unit tests.
Replays authentic mock datasets matching the canonical design prototype (design/K8s Monitor.dc.html).
Emulates live log tickers, cluster status latency fluctuations, and synthetic metric pulses.
data.benefits-of-the-seam#Benefits of the Sea:
Zero-Cluster UI Development: Frontend developers can design, style, and test complex features (such as CrashLoopBackOff log viewers or diff inspectors) entirely in a standard browser.
Hermetic Testing: Vitest and React Testing Library (RTL) tests run against MockProvider, ensuring lightning-fast test suites that never touch network sockets or external binaries.
Pixel-Fidelity Verification: Guarantees that design reviews and visual regression tests are completely deterministic.

data: To verify k7s against realistic live Kubernetes API server behaviors, the repository provides automated scripts to spin up a local kind (Kubernetes in Docker) fixture cluster.
data.bringing-up-the-fixture-cluster#Bringing:
# 1. Create kind cluster with standard workloads
./dev/cluster/up.sh
# 2. Or create with metrics-server enabled (populates CPU/MEM columns)
./dev/cluster/up.sh --metrics
# 3. Seed Helm fixture release
./dev/cluster/helm-fixture.sh
This sets up a context named kind-k7s-dev pre-populated with:
Multi-container pods (app + sidecar logging).
A CrashLoopBackOff pod reproducing realistic exit codes, crash restart counts, and error log lines.
A Pending pod unschedulable due to resource requests.
StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, CronJobs, Ingresses, NetworkPolicies, ConfigMaps, and Secrets.
A sample Helm release (fixture-app) with revision history for testing rollback and uninstall workflows.
data.running-live-verification-harnesses#Runn:
With the fixture cluster running:
# Build Rust example harnesses
cargo build --examples --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
# Run the manifested runner across fixtures
node dev/run-harnesses.mjs --fixtures kind,helm,metrics,multi

data: k7s provides safe, high-leverage administrative actions with clear blast-radius confirmations so you always know what will be affected before changes take place.
data.1-scaling-workloads#1. Scaling Workloads: Scale Deployments, StatefulSets, and ReplicaSets with immediate replica count adjustment and target replica preview.
data.2-rollout-restarts--undos#2. Rollout Res:
Rollout Restart: Triggers a rolling restart of pods (via annotation mutation) without downtime.
Rollout Undo (Rollback): Reverts Deployments, StatefulSets, or DaemonSets to a specific previous revision from their controller revision history.
data.3-pod-delete--eviction#3. Pod Delete & E:
Single-pod delete triggers graceful pod termination.
For crashlooping pods, option to delete immediately without grace period.
data.node-management--drain-pre-flight#Node M:
Administrative node operations are built with strict safety guards:
Cordon / Uncordon: Mark nodes unschedulable to prevent new pod placements.
Eviction-Based Drain:
Uses Kubernetes eviction API to ensure PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs) are honored.
PDB Disruption Pre-Flight Calculation: Before you confirm a drain, k7s analyzes all running pods against active PDBs to show if any budget would block the drain:
Node Drain Pre-Flight Analysis:
- Evictable Pods: 14
- DaemonSet Pods (Skipped): 3
- PDB 'api-pdb': 3/3 healthy, 1 disruption allowed [OK]
- PDB 'db-cluster-pdb': 1/1 healthy, 0 disruptions allowed [BLOCKED]
data.resource-creation-from-yaml#Resource Cre:
Click + Create (or press ⌘N) to open the Resource Creation Modal:
Create arbitrary Kubernetes resources from YAML or JSON.
Run a server-side dry-run validation to test permissions and field schemas before committing to the cluster.
data.multi-select--bulk-confirmations#Multi-S:
Select multiple resources using Shift + Click or ⌘ + Click.
Bulk actions (e.g. bulk delete or bulk restart) display an explicit confirmation modal listing every selected resource by name and namespace.

data: k7s provides a powerful, local-first multi-cluster management engine designed to keep multiple Kubernetes contexts connected and updated simultaneously.
data.the-cluster-rail--fast-switching-19#The:
The left sidebar features a compact Cluster Rail showing every connected cluster with its initials, color avatar, and worst-problem status tint:
Instant Switching: Press ⌘ + 1 through ⌘ + 9 (or click the cluster avatar) to switch active views instantly.
Retained State: Switching active clusters does not tear down background connections. Tables, watch streams, terminal tabs, and active port-forwards are preserved in memory.
Zero-Latency Navigation: Returning to a previously visited cluster renders immediately without waiting for API re-syncs.
data.adding--importing-kubeconfigs#Adding & I:
k7s supports discovering and importing kubeconfigs from multiple sources:
Automatic Discovery: Automatically detects all contexts in ~/.kube/config and any files referenced in your KUBECONFIG environment variable.
Native File Picker Import: Click + Add Cluster or select File → Import Kubeconfig… to select external kubeconfig files. Imported contexts are persisted across application restarts.
Cluster Health & Stale State: If a cluster becomes temporarily unreachable (e.g. VPN disconnection or network glitch), k7s marks the cluster as Stale (amber badge) rather than dropping rows, retaining existing cached data until the network recovers.
data.qr-code-context-export-mk7s-sync#QR Code:
To quickly export a cluster context to a mobile device running mk7s:
Open the Cluster Switcher menu.
Click the QR code icon (▣) on the target cluster row.
Scan the cycling QR code with your mobile camera to transfer the sanitized context credentials securely over local air-gap.

data: Press ⌘K (or Ctrl + K on Linux/Windows) from anywhere in the application to open the Command Palette.
data.visual-showcase#Visual Showcase: Command Palette with fzy-style fuzzy search across kinds, resources, and administrative actions.
data.fuzzy-search-engine#Fuzzy Search Engine:
Powered by an in-memory fzy-style fuzzy ranking algorithm (src/lib/fuzzy.ts), the Command Palette indexes:
Resource Kinds: Jump directly to Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, CRDs, etc.
Active Resources: Instantly search for specific pods, services, or workloads across all namespaces.
Cluster Actions: Switch clusters, open settings, toggle themes, create resources from YAML, or export diagnostics.
Keyboard-Driven: Navigate results with ↑ / ↓ or Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P and press Enter to execute. Press Esc to dismiss.

data: k7s includes native, zero-dependency Helm support decoded directly from Kubernetes storage Secrets without requiring the helm CLI to be installed on your machine.
data.visual-showcase#Visual Showcase: Helm Releases overview: Deployed revisions, chart versions, app versions, and revision detail inspection.
data.secret-based-helm-decoding#Secret-Based:
Helm stores release states inside cluster Secrets named sh.helm.release.v1.<release-name>.v<revision>.k7s's Rust backend (src-tauri/src/kube/helm.rs) decodes these Secrets directly:
Base64 & Gzip Decompression: Reads and parses compressed release manifests in Rust.
Values & Metadata: Extracts chart version, app version, deployed timestamp, user-supplied values, and computed values.
Credential Redaction: Automatically detects and redacts sensitive keys (passwords, tokens, private keys) in the Values panel.
Lists all deployed Helm releases, their current status (deployed, superseded, failed, uninstalled), and every Kubernetes object created by that release.
data.2-revision-history#2. Revision History: View complete revision history with timestamps, chart versions, and notes.
data.3-server-side-rollback#3. Server-Side Ro:
Roll back a Helm release to any prior revision:
Applies the target revision's manifest via Server-Side Apply.
Writes a new revision Secret following standard Helm conventions, maintaining bidirectional compatibility with the official helm CLI.
data.4-safe-uninstall#4. Safe Uninstall: Uninstalling a release enumerates all objects created by the chart before deleting them and cleaning up the release's revision Secrets.

data: k7s features an integrated kubectl Terminal (press ⌘T or click the statusbar terminal pill) that spawns a real PTY shell pre-configured for your active Kubernetes cluster.
data.visual-showcase#Visual Showcase: Integrated kubectl terminal (⌘T) running inside an isolated, single-context kubeconfig environment.
data.architectural-highlights#Architectural H:
Real PTY Allocation: Uses the portable-pty crate to allocate a native pseudo-terminal connected directly to your default shell (zsh, bash, fish, or powershell).
Isolated Single-Context Kubeconfig: When spawned, k7s writes a temporary, read-only (0600) single-context kubeconfig pointing directly at the active cluster and sets KUBECONFIG in the subshell environment. Any kubectl command you run targets the viewed cluster immediately without risk of mutating other contexts.
Login-Shell PATH Discovery: Resolves your full user login shell PATH at boot so that kubectl, kubectx, k9s, and custom exec plugins (such as gke-gcloud-auth-plugin or aws-iam-authenticator) work seamlessly inside the packaged application.
Cluster-Badged Multi-Tabs: Open multiple terminal tabs badged by cluster ID. Tabs and shells terminate cleanly when closed or when the cluster disconnects.

data: k7s provides a full-featured Port Forwarding Hub for routing local TCP traffic directly to Pods and Services running inside your Kubernetes cluster.
data.1-from-pods-or-services#1. From Pods or:
In any Pod or Service detail panel or context menu, click Port Forward….
Select target container port, choose a local port (or auto-assign a free random port), and click Start Forward.
data.2-the-forwards-management-workspace#2. T:
View all active and configured port-forwards across all clusters in a single dashboard.
Real-time connection status indicators (running, connecting, stopped, error).
One-Click Browser Launch: Click the link or open icon to launch http://localhost:<port> directly in your default browser.
Reconnect Presets: Save frequently used port-forward configurations as named presets to restart them in a single click whenever you reconnect to the cluster.

data.cluster-overview#Cluster Overview:
The Cluster Overview: Live control plane status, node allocation gauges, cluster-wide CPU/Memory utilization, and workload health breakdown.
The Cluster Overview provides an instant snapshot of overall cluster vitality:
Control Plane Status: Control plane version, live API latency measurement, and health condition indicators.
Node Allocation: Nodes ready vs total, node roles, and cluster-wide allocatable capacity.
Resource Pressure: Aggregate CPU and Memory usage percentages streamed via metrics.k8s.io.
Workload Summary: Instant counts of running, ready, pending, and degraded workload controllers.
data.the-problems-aggregator#The Problems Agg:
The Problems view aggregates CrashLoopBackOffs, Pending scheduling blocks, and eviction risks across the cluster in real time.
The Problems view automatically filters and aggregates anomalous conditions across all monitored namespaces:
CrashLoopBackOff & Error Pods: Immediate visibility into crashing containers, restart counts, and last exit codes.
Pending / Unschedulable Pods: Detects pods blocked on CPU/Memory requests, node selectors, or PVC bindings.
Eviction & Disruption Risks: Highlights pods with failing liveness probes or nodes under memory pressure.
data.dynamic-crd-discovery--printer-columns#D:
When connecting to a cluster, k7s queries the Kubernetes API discovery endpoint for installed CRDs:
Lazy Stream Spawning: CRD watch streams are opened lazily only when you navigate to that CRD's view, ensuring clusters with hundreds of CRDs don't consume unnecessary API server connections.
Additional Printer Columns: Respects the additionalPrinterColumns declared in the CRD manifest, rendering dynamic table columns (names, types, JSONPath values) just like kubectl get.

data: The main workspace in k7s features high-density, virtualized resource tables engineered for speed, flexibility, and precise data filtering.
data.visual-table-showcase#Visual Table Showc: Pods table with real-time stream status, namespace filtering, tone-colored health dots, and age formatting.
data.deployments-and-workload-tables#Deployme: Deployments table showing desired vs ready replicas, up-to-date counts, and age metrics.
data.1-virtualized-infinite-scrolling#1. Virt: Large production tables with thousands of items (e.g. 10,000 pods) scroll smoothly at 60fps. Only visible rows are rendered into the DOM, minimizing memory usage and CPU rendering cycles.
data.2-multi-level-filtering#2. Multi-Level F:
Namespace Selector: Filter by a single namespace or view resources across all namespaces.
Quick Text Filter (/): Press / to instantly filter rows by name, namespace, or status substring.
Label Selector Expressions: Filter tables using standard Kubernetes label expressions:
app=web, tier in (api, backend), !canary
data.3-column-customization--sorting#3. Colum:
Sorting: Click any column header to toggle ascending/descending sort with numeric and semantic age awareness.
Column Resizing & Reordering: Drag column dividers to adjust widths, or reorder columns via the table settings menu.
Custom JSONPath Columns: Add ad-hoc custom columns extracted via JSONPath directly from the resource definition (e.g. $.spec.serviceAccountName).
data.4-selection--bulk-actions#4. Selection &:
Keyboard Navigation: Navigate rows using j / k or arrow keys. Press Enter to open the detail panel.
Multi-Selection: Shift + Click to select contiguous ranges, or ⌘ + Click (Ctrl + Click) to toggle individual rows.
Bulk Operations: Right-click a multi-row selection to execute bulk deletions, restart rollouts, or cordon nodes.
data.5-csv-export#5. CSV Export: Click the export icon on any table toolbar to export the currently filtered view as a formatted CSV file.

data: Welcome to k7s! This guide covers everything you need to know to install, run, configure, and get productive with k7s.
data.system-requirements--prerequisites#Syste:
To build and run k7s from source, ensure your environment meets the following baseline prerequisites:
Requirement	Minimum Version	Notes	Node.js	>= 20.0.0	Node 20 or Node 22 recommended	Package Manager	pnpm >= 10.0.0 or npm >= 10.0.0	pnpm is the repository default	Rust Toolchain	Stable (>= 1.80.0)	Install via rustup	Tauri v2 Prerequisites	OS-dependent	Xcode CLI tools (macOS), webkit2gtk / build-essential (Linux), WebView2 (Windows)	Kubernetes Access	v1.24+	Any valid ~/.kube/config (or use demo mode)	Local Kind (Optional)	kind >= 0.20.0 + kubectl	For running the local end-to-end fixture cluster	
No Cluster Needed for Testing: You do not need a running Kubernetes cluster to try out k7s! You can launch k7s in Demo Mode (VITE_DEMO=1), which runs the full UI in your browser or desktop window with rich, synthetic fixture data.
data.quick-start-30-seconds#Quick Start (30 S:
Clone the repository and launch the app in demo mode right away:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/s4njee/k7s.git
cd k7s
# 2. Install dependencies
pnpm install # or npm install
# 3. Launch in Demo Mode (instant browser UI, no Rust build needed)
VITE_DEMO=1 pnpm dev
Visit http://localhost:1420 to interact with the full mock cluster.
data.running-against-a-real-kubernetes-cluste:
When you are ready to connect to real Kubernetes clusters:
# Recommended dev launcher (guards against stale ports and orphans)
dev/run.sh
# Or standard Tauri dev runner
pnpm tauri:dev
By default, k7s reads your current kubeconfig context at ~/.kube/config and connects immediately. You can also supply a custom kubeconfig path:
KUBECONFIG=/path/to/custom-kubeconfig.yaml dev/run.sh
data.next-steps#Next Steps:
Check out the full Installation Guide for pre-built binaries and native platform packages.
Learn about Demo Mode & Stress Testing.
Configure themes, log levels, and namespaces in Configuration & Preferences.

data: k7s is a fast, keyboard-light, single-window Kubernetes visual monitor in the spirit of Lens, built as a desktop application with a high-performance Rust backend (Tauri v2) and a React 19 + TypeScript frontend.Designed from the ground up for high fidelity, instant responsiveness, zero telemetry, and deep cluster inspection, k7s delivers the rich visual ergonomics of modern desktop tools while preserving the raw control and speed required by DevOps and SRE teams.
data.visual-showcase#Visual Showcase: The resource table: 31+ built-in resource kinds plus discovered CRDs, with live stream counts, delta updates, and backend-driven status coloring.
data.why-k7s#Why k7s?:
Engineered with Tauri v2 and Rust for minimal memory footprint (< 100MB RAM), fast cold starts, and buttery smooth 60fps virtualized tables handling 10,000+ objects.
Completely telemetry-free. No account logins, no cloud tracking, no analytics pinging back. Your kubeconfigs, cluster URLs, and tokens never leave your local machine.
Seamlessly switch between multiple Kubernetes clusters (⌘1–9). k7s retains state, live watch streams, terminals, and port-forwards concurrently across all connected clusters.
Multi-container interleaved streaming, follow/pause, previous container inspection for crash loops, since-time filtering, text search, and color-toned log levels.
Built-in CodeMirror 6 YAML editor with dry-run diff against Kubernetes validating and mutating webhooks before committing any change.
Cluster-scoped PTY terminal (⌘T) that spawns with your login shell PATH and an isolated single-context kubeconfig pointing directly at the active cluster.
data.key-capabilities-at-a-glance#Key Capabil:
Multi-Cluster Rail: Switch between dozens of clusters instantly without teardown. Connect multiple kubeconfig files, view aggregated problem summaries, and export context QR codes for mobile sync (mk7s).
Comprehensive Catalog: 31+ built-in kinds across Workloads, Network, Config, Storage, Cluster, and RBAC, plus dynamic Custom Resource Definition (CRD) lazy discovery with additionalPrinterColumns.
Relationship Graph & Properties: Deep "what is this wired to" relationship resolution. Pods link to ReplicaSets and Deployments, PVCs resolve to PVs, Secrets redact credentials safely, and Helm releases show full revision histories.
Root Node Debug Shell: Launch an interactive privileged debug pod that nsenters directly into the host namespaces with an explicit consent gate and auto-expiring deadline.
Port-Forwarding Hub: Manage pod and service forwards with reconnect presets, live status indicators, and one-click browser launch.
Helm Release Management: Inspect releases decoded directly from storage Secrets, view values, diff revisions, and execute safe rollbacks or uninstalls.
Safe Operations: Eviction-based node drains that calculate PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs) before execution, workload rollout restarts and undos, and bulk actions.
Offline & Self-Contained: Bundled fonts (IBM Plex Sans, JetBrains Mono), local design tokens, and instant theme switching (Dark / Light / System).
data.documentation-roadmap#Documentation Road:
Explore the comprehensive guides and references below:
Getting Started: Installation on macOS, Linux, and Windows, building from source, running in demo mode, and configuration.
Architecture & Internals: Deep dive into the Rust ClientManager, watcher delta pipelines, Tauri IPC contract, and Zustand state architecture.
Core Features: Detailed guides on multi-cluster switching, tables, log streaming, YAML dry runs, Helm, port forwarding, and kubectl terminal.
Operations & Security: Diagnostics bundles, sanitization, log levels, security posture, and auto-updates.
Development & Testing: Testing strategy, live cluster harnesses, kind fixture clusters, and accessibility verification.
Reference Guide: Complete keyboard shortcut cheatsheets, supported resource matrix, and troubleshooting tips.

data: k7s provides a robust diagnostic system to ensure troubleshooting is fast, simple, and safe to share without leaking sensitive cluster credentials.
data.log-architecture-two-sinks-one-stream#Lo:
src-tauri/src/logging.rs installs a tracing subscriber at startup that feeds two destinations simultaneously:
stderr: For development convenience (dev/run.sh / pnpm tauri:dev).
Rotating Log File: Stored under the platform app log directory (k7s.YYYY-MM-DD.log), rotated daily with at most 5 files retained.
data.live-log-levels#Live Log Levels: Adjust log verbosity live via Settings → Diagnostics → Log Level (error, warn, info, debug, trace). Changes take effect immediately without restarting the application.
data.frontend-error-forwarding#Frontend Error: Uncaught window errors, unhandled promise rejections, and React Error Boundary exceptions (src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx) are automatically captured and forwarded to the backend logger with full stack traces.
data.export-diagnostics-e#Export Diagnostics:
Select File → Export Diagnostics… (or press ⌘⇧E) to generate a scrubbed .zip archive containing:
k7s.log — The last 2 MB of the active log file.
versions.json — App version, OS, architecture, and connected context names.
settings.json — Persisted preferences with context names and local paths redacted.
boundary.txt — The last React ErrorBoundary stack trace (if any).
data.automated-redaction-engine#Automated Red:
Before writing the zip archive, all data passes through diagnostics::redact (src-tauri/src/diagnostics.rs):
Server URLs and IP endpoints are replaced with <redacted>.
Bearer tokens, API keys, and certificate base64 blobs are stripped.
Local user home paths (/Users/<username>, /home/<username>) are scrubbed.

data: k7s is built around strict local-first security guarantees, privacy by default, and defense in depth.
data.zero-telemetry-policy#Zero Telemetry Pol:
No Remote Tracking: k7s has zero Google Analytics, Segment, PostHog, Mixpanel, or telemetry collectors.
No User Accounts: No sign-up, email verification, or cloud accounts required.
Strictly Opt-In Crash Reporting: Crash reporting is disabled by default. If enabled, it only transmits crash backtraces to a user-configured endpoint (e.g. self-hosted GlitchTip).
data.security-hardening--isolation#Security H:
Content Security Policy (CSP): The webview operates under a strict CSP: default-src 'self'. Network connections are strictly constrained to local IPC channels.
No dangerouslySetInnerHTML: All resource names, annotations, and logs are rendered as escaped text nodes, preventing XSS injection even when viewing malicious pod manifests.
Redacted Secret Viewing: Secrets displayed in the Properties tab redact base64 values by default. Applying YAML to Secrets enforces safety checks.
Scanned Dependencies: Automated CI workflows enforce cargo audit and pnpm audit gates to prevent vulnerable dependencies from entering release bundles.

data: k7s features an integrated, cryptographic auto-update system powered by tauri-plugin-updater and GitHub Releases.
data.update-mechanism#Update Mechanism:
Passive Checks: Checks quietly for new versions on launch and periodically in the background.
Status Bar Badge: When a new update is available, a non-intrusive update indicator appears in the status bar.
Settings UI: Open Settings → Software Updates to view the current version, check for updates, or trigger a download and restart.
data.signature-verification#Signature Verific:
Updates are signed using an Ed25519 keypair independent of Apple's Developer ID:
The public key is embedded inside src-tauri/tauri.conf.json.
The release workflow signs the update bundle using TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY stored securely in GitHub Actions secrets.
The app verifies the cryptographic signature before unpacking any update payload, preventing tampering or unauthorized binary delivery.

data: Common troubleshooting steps, known gotchas, and frequently asked questions for k7s.
data.1-cluster-shows-stale-amber-badge#1. Clu:
Cause: k7s lost network connectivity to the Kubernetes API server (e.g. disconnected corporate VPN, sleep/wake cycle, or API server restart).
Behavior: k7s preserves all existing rows and cache so you don't lose context.
Resolution: Re-establish network/VPN connectivity. k7s's background health poller will automatically clear the stale state on the next successful probe.
data.2-kind-table-shows-0-rows-and-permission:
Cause: Your Kubernetes user/ServiceAccount lacks RBAC permissions (get, list, watch) for that specific resource kind.
Behavior: k7s does not crash other stream watchers. It isolates the forbidden kind and displays a warning banner.
Resolution: Verify your ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding configurations.
data.1-kubectl-command-not-found-in-integrate:
Cause: When launched from macOS Finder / GUI launcher, the application environment may not inherit shell profile paths (/usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, ~/.krew/bin).
Resolution: k7s resolves your user login shell PATH at boot. If you installed kubectl after launching k7s, restart k7s or run source ~/.zshrc inside the terminal tab.
data.2-node-shell-fails-with-privileged-pods-:
Cause: The target cluster enforces Pod Security Standards (restricted or baseline) that prevent privileged containers with host namespace access.
Resolution: Node debug shell requires cluster permissions to run privileged pods with hostPID: true and hostIPC: true.
data.how-do-i-share-logs-for-a-bug-report-saf:
Press ⌘⇧E (or choose File → Export Diagnostics…).
Save the .zip archive.
Attach the generated .zip to your GitHub issue. All tokens, private certificates, server URLs, and home directory paths are automatically scrubbed by k7s's redaction engine.

data: k7s is structured as a two-tier desktop architecture: a Rust backend running inside the Tauri v2 process and a React 19 + TypeScript frontend running inside the native OS webview.
data.architectural-principles#Architectural P:
Separation of Concerns via Provider Seam: The frontend never directly imports Tauri IPC primitives. All data operations flow through a strict DataProvider interface. This allows running the entire application in a standard browser with synthetic mock data (MockProvider) during development or test execution.
Multi-Cluster Concurrent Lifecycle: Unlike traditional clients that tear down all state when switching clusters, k7s's ClientManager maintains concurrent cluster connections. Watch streams, terminal sessions, and port-forwards continue running in the background for connected clusters.
Delta-Driven Updates: To scale gracefully to clusters with over 10,000 objects, watchers accumulate change events and stream minimal upserts and deletes keyed by object uid rather than re-serializing massive full-snapshot arrays on every debounce tick.
Backend-Driven Status & Coloring Semantics: All complex Kubernetes status logic (waiting container reasons, exit codes, restart thresholds, ready counts, condition probes) is evaluated in Rust and serialized as a semantic tone (default, muted, ok, warn, err). The frontend remains dumb and maps tones directly to CSS design tokens.
Zero Webview Leaks & Hardened Sandboxing: Strict Content Security Policy (CSP), scoped Tauri capabilities, no dynamic HTML evaluation (dangerouslySetInnerHTML is strictly prohibited), and automatic sanitization of sensitive tokens in diagnostics.

data: The k7s backend (src-tauri/) is built in Rust using Tokio, the kube crate ecosystem, and Tauri v2.
data.key-responsibilities#Key Responsibilitie:
Kubeconfig Discovery & Merging: Reads ~/.kube/config, custom KUBECONFIG env paths, and imported standalone configs.
Connection Isolation: Each cluster connection (ClusterConnection) holds its own kube::Client, tokio watcher handles, metrics background pollers, active port-forwards, and open log streams.
Non-Destructive Switching: Switching the active cluster in the UI does not destroy background watchers for other clusters; it simply updates the active stream subscriptions.
Graceful Teardown: Disconnecting a single cluster aborts only its associated tasks without affecting other connected clusters.
data.watcher-pipeline--delta-engine#Watcher P:
For each monitored Kubernetes resource kind, k7s spawns a Tokio task wrapping kube::runtime::watcher:
Reflector Store: Ingests Applied, Deleted, and Restarted watch events.
Debouncing (~150ms): Groups bursts of high-frequency events (e.g. during a massive rollout) into single batches.
Delta vs Snapshot Emission:
On Initial Watch / Re-sync: Emits a complete snapshot payload containing all current rows.
On Steady State: Emits a minimal delta payload with arrays of upserts: Row[] and deletes: string[] (UIDs).
IPC Channel Namespacing: Events are published over namespaced Tauri event topics: resource-update:{cid}.
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Clone)]
#[serde(tag = "type")]
pub enum ResourceUpdatePayload {
    Snapshot { kind: String, rows: Vec<RowDto> },
    Delta { kind: String, upserts: Vec<RowDto>, deletes: Vec<String> },
}
data.dto-mapping--semantic-tones#DTO Mapping:
The backend parses raw Kubernetes OpenAPI resources into lightweight, frontend-ready Data Transfer Objects (RowDto in src-tauri/src/kube/dto.rs and mappers.rs):
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Clone)]
pub struct RowDto {
    pub uid: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub namespace: Option<String>,
    pub creation_ts: Option<i64>,
    pub cells: Vec<CellDto>,
    pub pod_meta: Option<PodMetaDto>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Clone)]
pub struct CellDto {
    pub text: String,
    pub tone: Tone, // Default | Muted | Ok | Warn | Err
}
data.tone-rules#Tone Rules::
Ok (Green): Pods Running, Nodes Ready, Deployments with replicas == available, DaemonSets 100% scheduled.
Warn (Amber): Pods Pending or ContainerCreating, partially ready workloads (e.g. 1/2 ready), Scaling limited.
Err (Red): Pods in CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, or Error; restarts count > 5.
Muted (Gray): Namespace column, relative ages, completed jobs.
data.typed-error-envelopes-apperror#Typed Err:
Rather than passing raw, unformatted error strings across the IPC bridge, k7s serializes failures as a typed AppError (src-tauri/src/error.rs):
{
  "code": "PERMISSION_DENIED",
  "message": "Permission denied: unable to list resource 'secrets' in namespace 'prod'.",
  "retryable": true,
  "action": "Check RBAC ClusterRoleBindings for your user context.",
  "detail": "HTTP 403 Forbidden: secrets is forbidden: User cannot list resource"
}
This contract ensures the frontend can display user-friendly remediation messages while reserving raw technical details for expandable debug views.

data: Clicking any row or pressing Enter opens the side Detail Panel, providing deep inspection tabs tailored to the selected resource kind.
data.1-logs-tab#1. Logs Tab:
Real-time streaming logs with container switching, level toning, search filtering, and since-time windows.
Live Streaming & Pause: Real-time log streaming with auto-scroll lock. Clicking Pause stops stream consumption and locks the scroll position for inspection.
Multi-Container Switching: Instantly switch between containers or view interleaved logs across multi-container pods and sidecars.
Previous Container Logs: Read logs from the previous container instance (previous: true) to diagnose CrashLoopBackOff crashes and exit codes.
Since Windows & Timestamps: Filter logs by time windows (e.g. 5m, 15m, 1h) and toggle RFC3339 timestamp prefixes.
Smart Level Toning: Log lines are parsed into semantic levels (INFO in blue, WARN in amber, ERROR in red, DEBUG in gray).
Save to File: Export the current log buffer directly to a local text file.
data.2-properties-tab#2. Properties Tab:
The Properties inspector resolves live references (e.g. Pod -> ReplicaSet -> Deployment, Secrets, ConfigMaps).
The Properties tab answers "What is this object actually wired to?":
Resolved Hyperlinks: References are resolved live against the cluster. A Pod's owner link resolves through its ReplicaSet to the parent Deployment; a Service link resolves to backing Endpoints and Pods; an Ingress links to TLS Secrets and Services.
Missing References Called Out: Unresolved links are explicitly flagged as (not found) rather than failing silently or 404ing.
Live Metadata Editor: Directly add, edit, or delete Labels and Annotations without writing raw YAML.
Safe Secrets Inspection: Secret keys are listed with encoded sizes; values are redacted server-side by default with explicit click-to-reveal controls.
data.3-yaml-tab--server-side-dry-run#3. YAML:
CodeMirror 6 YAML editor with token-matched syntax highlighting and dry-run validation.
CodeMirror 6 Editor: Fast, responsive YAML editing with full syntax highlighting, indentation guides, and line numbers.
Server-Side Dry Run: Before applying changes, k7s executes a server-side dry run (dryRun=All) to validate mutations against cluster admission controllers and webhooks.
Diff Preview: Displays an exact visual diff of mutating webhook changes and defaultings before committing.
Inline API Error Reporting: Validation errors (e.g. immutable field violations) are highlighted directly in the editor with API error messages verbatim.
data.4-diff-tab#4. Diff Tab:
Diff inspector comparing live runtime object against last-applied-configuration or managed-fields baseline.
Side-by-side and inline diff visualizer.
Identifies cluster mutations introduced by controllers, webhooks, or manual edits.
data.5-events-tab--canvas-timeline#5. Events:
Events tab with color-coded Normal and Warning event cards and timestamps.
Event Cards: Categorized by Normal (green) and Warning (red), displaying reason, message, count, and last seen timestamp.
Canvas Event Timeline: An interactive visual timeline plotting cluster events over time with zoom and pan capabilities.
data.6-metrics--pod-sparklines#6. Metrics & P:
Plotly metrics charts with Prometheus PromQL backfilling and node filesystem utilization.
Pod Sparklines: Real-time CPU and Memory sparkline charts overlaid with declared requests and limits.
Node Exporter Integration: Detailed node metrics (CPU cores, memory distribution, network I/O, and disk filesystem utilization sorted fullest-first).
Prometheus Backfilling: When Prometheus is detected, queries historical PromQL data to backfill time-series charts across historical hours.
data.7-topology-dag-tab#7. Topology DAG Tab:
Resource Topology DAG visualizing relationship hierarchies across workloads, services, and endpoints.
Visual Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) charting relationships from Ingresses → Services → Endpoints → Pods → PVCs → Nodes.
data.8-interactive-shell--node-root-debug-she:
Interactive container exec shell powered by xterm.js.
Container Exec Shell: Full interactive TTY shell into any running container powered by xterm.js and Tauri PTY streams.
Node Root Debug Shell: Launch a root debug shell into any Kubernetes worker node. Spawns a privileged pod pinned to the target node running nsenter into host namespaces, protected by an explicit security consent screen and an auto-terminating server deadline.

data: k7s stores user configuration and runtime settings locally in a lightweight JSON file without requiring any cloud synchronization or remote accounts.
data.visual-showcase#Visual Showcase: Settings panel: Appearance, default namespace, log levels, updater controls, and opt-in diagnostics.
data.settings-panel-#Settings Panel (⌘,): Press ⌘ + , (or Ctrl + , on Linux/Windows) or select File → Settings… to open the Settings panel.
data.1-appearance--theme#1. Appearance & Them:
Theme Mode:
System (Default): Automatically synchronizes with your OS appearance (Dark/Light mode).
Dark: Fixed dark theme (#0d0d0f background, #121214 panels, high-contrast dark syntax highlighting).
Light: Clean light theme with bright work areas, dark sidebar accents, and token-derived terminal/chart palettes.
Table Density & Typography: Adjust row padding, font sizes, and mono font preferences.
data.2-general-preferences#2. General Prefere:
Default Namespace: Set the default namespace filter on initial cluster connection (e.g. default, all, or a team namespace).
Log Buffer Limit: Maximum number of lines retained in the ring buffer per log stream (default: 200 lines, configurable up to 5,000 lines).
Auto-Updates: Toggle background daily update checks and automatic download notifications.
data.3-diagnostics--telemetry#3. Diagnostics:
Log Level: Dynamically change the backend logging verbosity (error, warn, info, debug, trace) without restarting the application.
Crash Reporting: Strictly opt-in panic/error reporting to a user-configured endpoint (e.g. GlitchTip or Sentry). Off by default.
data.file-locations#File Locations:
Configuration files and runtime logs are stored in standardized platform directories:
Platform	Preferences (prefs.json)	Application Logs (k7s.YYYY-MM-DD.log)	macOS	~/Library/Application Support/io.k7s.app/	~/Library/Logs/io.k7s.app/	Linux	~/.config/io.k7s.app/ (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME)	~/.config/io.k7s.app/logs/	Windows	%APPDATA%\io.k7s.app\	%APPDATA%\io.k7s.app\logs\
data.environment-variables#Environment Variab:
Developers and operators can control runtime behavior using the following environment variables:
Variable	Description	KUBECONFIG	Explicit path(s) to kubeconfig file(s), overriding the default ~/.kube/config. Supports colon-delimited (:) on Unix and semicolon-delimited (;) on Windows.	RUST_LOG	Overrides the startup logging level in development mode (e.g. RUST_LOG=debug,k7s_lib=trace).	VITE_DEMO	When set to 1, boots the frontend in demo mock mode (MockProvider).	VITE_STRESS	When used with VITE_DEMO=1, specifies the number of synthetic pods to generate (e.g. VITE_STRESS=5000).	WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER	On Linux, disables DMA-BUF renderer to prevent black screens in headless or nested VM environments.

data: k7s features an integrated Demo Mode (MockProvider) that runs the entire frontend in isolation without requiring a Rust compiler, a Tauri runtime, or a live Kubernetes cluster.
data.why-demo-mode#Why Demo Mode?:
Rapid UI/UX Iteration: Work on CSS styles, layouts, animations, and component behavior inside standard web browser devtools (Chrome/Firefox/Safari) at http://localhost:1420.
Pixel-Fidelity Testing: Replays exact reference mock datasets matching the canonical design prototype (design/K8s Monitor.dc.html).
Zero Cluster Overhead: Great for presentations, demos, design reviews, or onboarding contributors who don't have local Kubernetes clusters configured.
Stress-Testing Engine: Simulate large-scale production clusters with thousands of synthetic pods to test virtualization and scrolling performance.
data.launching-demo-mode#Launching Demo Mode:
To launch demo mode in a browser:
# Standard demo mode
VITE_DEMO=1 pnpm dev
Open http://localhost:1420 in your browser.
data.stress-testing-virtualization#Stress Tes:
By default, demo mode loads 13 representative pods illustrating various Kubernetes lifecycle states (Running, Pending, CrashLoopBackOff, Completed, Terminating).To test k7s under massive cluster load (such as 5,000 or 10,000 pods):
# Generate 5,000 synthetic pods
VITE_DEMO=1 VITE_STRESS=5000 pnpm dev
This exercises the virtualized table windowing algorithm (src/components/table/useVirtualRows.ts), proving that DOM nodes remain capped at ~40 rows and scroll frame rates remain pinned at 60fps.
data.included-mock-fixtures#Included Mock Fix:
The MockProvider (src/providers/mock/) simulates realistic cluster state:
Fixture Area	Simulated Data	Multi-Cluster	Three connected contexts: freya (production), odin-staging (staging), and loki-dev (development).	Namespaces	all, prod, staging, monitoring, kube-system.	Workloads	Diverse Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, and CronJobs.	Chaos Pods	heimdall-auth-7b8f9c-2xk9 (CrashLoopBackOff with real error logs and restarts count), canary-ingress-worker (Pending due to resource constraints).	Live Log Ticker	Simulates active log streaming ticking every ~900ms with formatted JSON logs, timestamps, and multi-level toning (INFO/WARN/ERROR/DEBUG).	YAML & Events	Real manifests and Kubernetes warning/normal events tied to each mock object.	Cluster Metrics	Live CPU/Memory percentages, API latency simulation (~42ms), and node counts (6/6 Ready).

data: k7s is distributed as standalone desktop application bundles for macOS, Linux, and Windows, and can also be built directly from source.
data.pre-built-binaries#Pre-Built Binaries: Download official signed packages from the GitHub Releases page:
data.undefined#macOS (.dmg / .app):
k7s supports Apple Silicon (arm64) and Intel (x86_64) architectures.
Download k7s_<version>_aarch64.dmg or k7s_<version>_x64.dmg.
Open the .dmg and drag k7s.app into your /Applications folder.
Launch k7s from Spotlight or Launchpad.
Gatekeeper Notice: On initial release before Developer ID notarization is attached, macOS may prompt with "k7s can't be opened because it is from an unidentified developer." Right-click k7s.app, select Open, and confirm Open on the prompt dialog.
data.undefined#Linux (.AppImage / .deb / .rpm:
k7s is packaged as a universal AppImage as well as native .deb and .rpm installers.AppImage:
chmod +x k7s_<version>_amd64.AppImage
./k7s_<version>_amd64.AppImage
Debian / Ubuntu (.deb):
sudo dpkg -i k7s_<version>_amd64.deb
Fedora / RHEL (.rpm):
sudo rpm -i k7s_<version>_x86_64.rpm
WebKitGTK Note: On Linux systems running under headless or virtualized GPU environments, if you encounter webview render glitches, pass WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 k7s.
data.undefined#Windows (.msi / .exe):
k7s is built for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit).
Download k7s_<version>_x64-setup.exe or k7s_<version>_x64.msi.
Run the installer and follow the setup wizard.
Launch k7s from your Start Menu.
WebView2 Requirement: Windows 11 includes Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime by default. If running on an older Windows 10 build, ensure the Evergreen WebView2 Runtime is installed.
data.building-from-source#Building from Sourc: To compile k7s from source, ensure you have Rust, Node.js, and Tauri dependencies installed.
data.1-install-os-dependencies#1. Install OS:
# Install Xcode Command Line Tools
xcode-select --install
# Ensure Rust is installed
rustup update stable
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
  libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev
rustup update stable
sudo dnf groupinstall "C Development Tools and Libraries"
sudo dnf install -y webkit2gtk4.1-devel openssl-devel libappindicator-gtk3-devel librsvg2-devel
rustup update stable
# Install C++ build tools via Visual Studio Installer
# Ensure Rust (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) is installed

data.2-build-the-application#2. Build the App:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/s4njee/k7s.git
cd k7s
# Install frontend dependencies
pnpm install
# Run typecheck and tests
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
# Compile production binary and installer
pnpm run tauri:build
The output artifacts will be placed in src-tauri/target/release/bundle/.
